summary.text: A 90-year-old man with complete heart block had a left-sided dual-chamber pacemaker inserted 8 years earlier and a right-sided dual-chamber pacemaker 3 years earlier because of lead insulation failure and noise, with explantation of the left-sided box; he had four pacing leads in situ. Past history included coronary artery bypass surgery, hypertension, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, hyperthyroidism and mild aortic stenosis.

He presented with new-onset intermittent dizziness; the electrocardiogram showed complete heart block and a pacing check showed right ventricular lead failure with loss of capture. A temporary pacing wire was inserted via the right femoral vein and a temporary externalized VVIR pacemaker implanted.

Blood tests were unremarkable with normal electrolytes and echocardiography showed a normal-sized left ventricle, ejection fraction 55%, and mild aortic stenosis and tricuspid regurgitation. Strategies for a permanent system, including another right-sided dual-chamber pacemaker with potential laser lead extraction, were discussed.

A Micra atrioventricular leadless pacemaker was implanted under local anaesthetic and sedation via right femoral venous access, programmed to VDI at 50 b.p.m., tracking the atrial-paced rhythm from the existing right-sided device. There were no immediate complications and he was discharged home the following day.
At 6 weeks of follow-up the pacing check showed appropriate atrioventricular tracking with AM-VP and VP frequencies of 86.9% and 12.8%; the underlying rhythm was complete heart block.
